full_judgment:
2. The petitioner filed a miscellaneous case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption of the case land. The jote was sold by the opposite party No. 2 in favour of opposite party No. 1 on 21.9.92 by registered deed of sale. The petitioner having not informed about the sale and no notice having been served upon him he filed the pre-emption case within time upon depositing the consideration amount of Tk. 3000/- and as compensation amount of Tk. 300/- and in total Tk. 3,300/-. 

 4. It is stated by the opposite parties that opposite party No. 2 the seller approached the pre-emptor petitioner 6 months before the alleged sale for selling the land to him but owing to financial inability he expressed his inability to buy the case land rather he helped the purchaser in purchasing the land. He was also present at the time of delivery of possession as such the learned Judges of the Courts below held that by conduct the pre-emptor has established that he gave up his claim of right of exercising the pre-emption by clear acquiescence as such the case is barred by principle of estoppel. Both the Court referred two decisions of the Appellate Division being 44 DLR.(AD)62 and 42DLR(AD)189. In the case of Akhlasur Rahman and others Vs. Safarullah and others reported in 42 DLR(AD) 189 it is held. 

 In this case the facts on which waiver has been established is that the seller approached the pre-emptor for selling out his land some 6 months ago but he expressed his inability to purchase the land on the ground of financial crisis. Whether such expression of inability of financial crisis would debar him from exercising his legal right of pre-emption is a question to be scrutinized. O.P.W. 14 has stated in his cross-examination that 5/6 days before the registration his brother opposite party No. 2 (the seller) talked about the selling of the land and he further has stated on what date the pre-emptor has expressed his inability to purchase the land he cannot say. Opposite party No. 2 in his cross-examination has stated he could not remember the date of talk about the sale of the land but has stated that 5/6 months before the registration of the sale deed he talked with the pre-emptor. On these fact the Court found that the case is barred by principle of acquiescence and waiver but the decision reported in 44 DLR (AD) 62 has clearly stated, 

 "His failure to procure money to purchase the land cannot take away his right if he can come up within time" and admittedly the pre-emptor petitioner has filed the case within limitation. Therefore, the inability to purchase the case land would not amount to waiver or acquiescence. The learned Judges also stated that the pre-emptor—petitioner was present at the time of delivery of possession as such his right to purchase the property under section 96 is barred. It is not also a valid ground for debarring him from purchasing the land and in exercising his statutory right of pre-emption. Expressing his inability to purchase the case land on the ground of financial inability would mean that his right to purchase has been kept in abeyance for a particular time. The moment he collected the money he filed the case for pre-emption. The Judges of the Appellate Division in the case of Akhlasur Rahman and others vs. Safarullah and others reported in 42 DLR(AD)189 has pronounced a note of caution by observing that any and every act touching the transaction in which the pre-emptor may have taken part or the mere fact of knowledge about the transfer or temporary unwillingness on his part to buy cannot debar him from claiming his right at the proper time. Therefore, when the preemptor's inability to purchase the and on the ground of financial inability which was a temporary one will not operate as estoppel from purchasing the land and exercise his right of pre-emption. It is a question of proper inference to be drawn in a particular, case when such plea of acquiescence would be applied or not. In this case the Courts below have not properly assessed the evidence and facts on record and jumped to a conclusion that the case is barred by principle of acquiescence and waiver. Therefore, the judgment and order passed by the Courts below are liable to be set aside.
